summary: Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1980. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1991) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).

Rong Ma works in Tibetology and other fields. He earned a doctorate in social geography from Brown University, served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University, and was Director of the Institute of Sociology and Anthropology at Peking University (attested 1998).

Rongdao Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University (attested 2013) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, and was a visiting fellow at the Center for Chinese Studies.

Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.
Rory Mackenzie works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Peter Harvey and held a teaching post at International Christian College.
Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University circa 1960-1969. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from circa 1987 to 2012.

Rosane Rocher is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Free University of Brussels (ca. 1955-1965). She served at the University of Pennsylvania as a professor (ca. 1970-2005) and became Professor Emerita of South Asia Studies around 2005.

Rosemarie Fuchs is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (attested 2000). She was attested in 2000 as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee.
Rosemarie Lühr is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She held academic posts at the University of Giessen from circa 1990 to 1993 and at the University of Jena from circa 1993 to 2012.

Rosina Pastore is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere. She also served as an assistant and PhD candidate at the University of Lausanne.
Roy Rappaport was a scholar of religious studies and anthropology who studied at Columbia University (ca. 1959-1966). He served on the faculty at the University of Michigan from circa 1965 to 1997.

Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University (ca. 1997-2004) and earned his PhD at Columbia University (ca. 2005-2011) under Gary A. Tubb, later joining Tel Aviv University around 2011.

Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard (ca. 1953-1957) and Columbia (ca. 1965-1977), and held posts at the University of Oslo (ca. 1983-1989) and the Australian National University (ca. 1990-2000).
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held a post there.

Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (ca. 1973-1978) under Akira Hirakawa and Jikido Takasaki, and held posts at Sophia University (ca. 1978-1989) and Southern Methodist University (from ca. 1989; professor ca. 2002).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied theology at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald and in Paris under Eugène Burnouf. He held a professorship at the University of Tübingen from 1848 to 1895.

Ruixuan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University (attested 2018) under Paul Harrison and held a post at Heidelberg University.

Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (ca. 1935-1939) and Harvard University (ca. 1939-1942), and held a post at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.

Rupert Gethin is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester (ca. 1982-1987) under Lance S. Cousins, became Co-Director of Bristol's Centre for Buddhist Studies (ca. 1987), and was Pali Text Society President in 2003.

Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nagoya University. Attested in 2015, she held researcher posts at the Eastern Institute and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
